scope: Papers with open-access full text or substantive excerpts retrieved via search

papers_with_full_access.title: Introducing the Model Fidelity Metric (MFM) for robust and diagnostic land surface model evaluation
key_findings: MFM constructed from robust statistics (median absolute deviation) and information theory
Measures three components: accuracy (error), variability (amplitude), distribution similarity
Evaluated against NSE and KGE using synthetic case studies designed to isolate failure modes
MFM is more robust than NSE/KGE in low-variability catchments and extreme cases
Applied to large-sample hydrological dataset (land surface model evaluation)
papers_with_full_access.gap_assessment: Proposes a combined error+variability metric (B+A partially) but not C (recall of extremes), not D (joint selection rule), not E (decision-change quantification), not G (air quality), not in EMS

papers_with_full_access.title: Standard assessments of climate forecast skill can be misleading
key_findings: Hindcast-based skill assessments tend to overestimate real forecast skill
Model skill rankings change when moving from hindcast to real forecast settings
Bias-correction choices drive differences between apparent and real skill
El Niño-Southern Oscillation application demonstrates ranking reversals across criteria
papers_with_full_access.gap_assessment: Documents ranking reversal (addresses E partially) but in climate context; no joint error+fidelity rule; not EMS; not air quality

papers_with_full_access.title: Rolling-Origin Validation Reverses Model Rankings in Multi-Step PM10 Forecasting
key_findings: Uses 2350 daily PM10 observations 2017-2024 from southern Spain (single station)
Compares XGBoost and SARIMA against persistence under static split and rolling-origin protocol
Rolling-origin evaluation reverses rankings: XGBoost inconsistent at short/medium horizons, SARIMA positive-skilled across all horizons
Horizon-specific skill profile shown for 1-7 day ahead
Authors: Garcia Crespi, Yubero Funes, Alfosea Simon (UMH)
papers_with_full_access.gap_assessment: Addresses H (rolling-origin), G (PM10), A (error/skill criterion), E partially (ranking reversal documented); does NOT address B (variance retention alpha), C (recall extremes), D (joint rule), F (multi-station); not yet in EMS

full_text_gap_conclusion: Among papers with full-text access, none combines error criterion + variance retention + recall of extremes as a unified model selection rule. P005 is the closest in domain (PM10) and methodology (rolling-origin) but lacks the joint fidelity criteria that define Paper A's contribution. P003 is closest conceptually (combined error+variability metric) but in hydrology and outside EMS.
